summary.en: Recent cross-border fighting saw Pakistani security forces repel an infiltration, killing one Pakistani soldier and twelve militants, including Afghan Taliban fighters, while Pakistan warned the Taliban to stop using Afghan soil for attacks. A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport killed a Pakistani national and wounded eleven others, prompting regional condemnation. The Taliban are now leveraging European anti-migrant sentiment, and Afghanistan announced a potential China trade route to the Persian Gulf. The conflict remains deadly, with 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Nylig så grenseoverskridende kamper at pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker avviste en infiltrasjon, og drepte en pakistansk soldat og tolv militante, inkludert afghanske taliban-krigere, mens Pakistan advarte talibanene om å slutte å bruke afghansk jord for angrep. Et houthi-missilangrep på Riyadh-flyplassen drepte en pakistansk nasjonal og såret elleve andre, noe som førte til regional fordømmelse. Taliban utnytter nå europeisk anti-migrasjons-stemning, og Afghanistan kunngjorde en potensiell kinesisk handelsrute til Persiabukta. Konflikten forblir dødelig, med 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
